name: session-control
description: Session-control orchestrator mod: a side panel (/session-control) over the worker registry, queued work and open points, completion classification, launch/acknowledge/retire tools for workers, bookkeeping tools for the helper files, licence tools (list_licences, probe_licence_usage and launch_worker's config_dir: licences found by the presence of their files only, usage as the CLI shows it, no credential read), a secret scan of worker results, a prompt lint and a sign-off guard for worker launches, and a sign-off guard on the orchestrator's own git commands.

orchestratorDir.title: Orchestrator directory
orchestratorDir.description: Directory holding the orchestrator's CLAUDE.md and helper files. Empty: the mod uses the session's directory when its CLAUDE.md starts with '# Role: Session Orchestrator' and does nothing elsewhere.

registryPath.title: Worker registry
registryPath.description: The headless-session registry (a JSON array of entries). A leading ~ is the home directory.

completionWrites.title: Write completions to the registry
completionWrites.description: When a worker's pid is gone, merge its outcome into its registry entry in place (drop pid, reported=false).

pollSeconds.title: Poll interval (seconds)
pollSeconds.description: How often the session state is gathered.

runsDir.title: Worker run files
runsDir.description: Directory for the result and error files of launched workers (outside any repo). A leading ~ is the home directory.

licencePickCommand.title: Licence picker command
licencePickCommand.description: Command that chooses the licence for a fresh worker launch. {need} is replaced by the headroom percent; a leading ~/ is expanded. It prints one absolute config directory and exits 0, or exits 3 when no licence has room. Empty: workers start with the machine's default config directory (~/.claude). A launch given an explicit config_dir (a discovered licence) does not run it.

debug.title: Debug trace
debug.description: Write a JSON-lines trace of the mod's events, commands, file writes, verdicts and errors to trace.log in the runs directory (rotated at 2 MiB, 3 files kept; no file contents, prompts or credentials). The environment variable SESSION_CONTROL_DEBUG=1 switches it on too.

nodePath.title: Node executable
nodePath.description: The node executable the mod's helper runs with: Node.js 22 or newer, which the mod needs for every file and process operation (a leading ~/ is the home directory). Empty: node from the PATH.

launchRoute.title: Launch route
launchRoute.description: bash: workers start through the Bash tool (on native Windows Claude Code offers it only when it finds Git Bash). powershell: on native Windows workers start through the PowerShell tool instead (claude.exe started by Start-Process, the prompt on standard input from the prompt file); on Linux and WSL the option changes nothing. Any other value counts as bash.

notices.title: Notices
notices.description: on: the poll-based notices (orphan, stall, queue-ready, unit-complete, compliance-due, open-point-age, retire-due, repo-state, lock-holder, registry-unreadable, mod-drift, secret-in-result, finished-open) reach the model with the next prompt, as a toast and in the debug trace. off: none of them; the completion notes stay, and so does the drift band above the prompt (modSource off hides it). Any other value counts as on.

modSource.title: Source mod folder
modSource.description: The mod folder the loaded mod is compared with (hooks, helper, types and .claude-plugin/plugin.json, by content hash, at the start and every 5 minutes); while they differ a dim line above the prompt says so and how to reload. A leading ~ is the home directory. Empty: <orchestrator directory>/mod when it exists, else no band. off: no band.

lockDirs.title: Lock folders
lockDirs.description: Comma separated absolute folders whose direct children are locks (a folder with a pid, owner or holder file, a *.pid or *.lock file; plain or JSON with a pid field). A lock whose holder pid is no longer alive is told once by the lock-holder notice; the mod never touches a lock. Empty: off.

licenceDirs.title: Licence folders
licenceDirs.description: Comma separated absolute config directories the licence tools (list_licences, probe_licence_usage, launch_worker's config_dir) count as licences besides the ones they find (the default directory, ~/.claude, ~/.claude/<name>, ~/.claude-<name>). A leading ~ is the home directory. Each counts only when it holds both .credentials.json and .claude.json as regular files (an entry that is a symbolic link to such a folder counts), a test of presence and kind only: neither file is opened. Empty: none.

desktopPaneScroll.title: Desktop pane scrolling
desktopPaneScroll.description: How the panel's sections scroll in Claude Desktop, whose pane shows a scroll bar of its own whenever its body can move (the terminal is not affected). spare: the panel stands between 8 blank rows above and below, so the wheel scrolls the sections; the pane's bar shows with its thumb in the middle. overflow: the same rows only while a section has more rows than it shows; no pane bar otherwise. minimal: 1 blank row above and below; the pane's thumb fills its track but for a row's height at each end. overflow-minimal: 1 row, only while a section has more rows than it shows. buttons: no blank rows and no pane bar; each such section gets an up and a down button, the wheel scrolls nothing. drag: no blank rows and no pane bar; each such section's scroll bar is a slider to drag (and the arrow, page, home and end keys after a click on it), the wheel scrolls nothing. page: no window at all; the three sections are drawn whole one below the other and the pane's own bar and wheel scroll the whole panel; no section scrolls by itself, a list shows at most 50 rows and the log its latest 100 lines. sections: three fixed boxes as tall as the pane, nothing scrolls; a box with more lines than it shows ends on a +N more line and has a [+] that draws that section alone as a page the pane's bar and wheel scroll, between title strips at the top and the bottom (another title switches, [-] returns); an open log is a box of two thirds showing its newest lines, and its [+] draws the whole log as such a page, started at its end. Any other value counts as spare.

desktopStyle.title: Desktop panel look
desktopStyle.description: The colours of the panel's sections view in Claude Desktop (desktopPaneScroll sections; every other value and the terminal draw plain). tint-soft: each section's box on a low-contrast tint of its hue, its title row starting on a bar of that hue. plain: no colour of its own. Hues: sessions blue, queued work violet, open points sand, the log grey. The section shown alone has its title marked in the strip with its colour. Dark mode only: a plugin's tree cannot tell which theme Desktop shows. Any other value counts as tint-soft.

desktopIcons.title: Desktop panel icons
desktopIcons.description: How the sections view in Claude Desktop draws its [+], [-] and [x]: text, or svg, drawn icons in the colours of the desktopStyle look (a plus, a minus or a cross of 2 px bars, inside the outline box or a frame of its own under plain buttons), each one row tall, pressed as the text ones. Any other value counts as text.

desktopPreview.title: Desktop panel preview
desktopPreview.description: A fixed sample state the sections view draws in Claude Desktop (desktopPaneScroll sections, docked) instead of the live one, to look at a combination of desktopStyle, desktopIcons, desktopButtons and desktopFont without any click: overview (three sessions, ten queued tasks in three project groups, three open points, none expanded), queue (the queued work expanded, its first group open), points (the open points expanded, the first selected), log (a running session's log of 40 lines expanded), empty (nothing at all), animate (the overview's data with the first queue group open and the first open point selected, looping by itself while the panel is shown: for sessions, then queued work, then open points, the three boxes for 2.4 s, the expand in the steps of desktopAnimation, the page for 2.4 s, the collapse; one loop takes 22.8 s under smooth, 14.4 s under off). It reads, writes and calls nothing, and its presses do nothing; every other desktopPaneScroll value, the panel seated inline and the terminal keep the live state. off: the live state. Any other value counts as off.

desktopGap.title: Desktop panel gap
desktopGap.description: The space between the three boxes of the sections view in Claude Desktop (desktopPaneScroll sections, docked), and on an expanded page between its title strip, its box and the strip's wrapped rows, in CSS pixels at Desktop's default density (a 19 px line): 2 by default; 0 lets them touch as before. Desktop sizes the gap in half lines, so it follows the person's density: 2 is 1.8 px with 17 px lines and 2.3 px with 22 px lines. The boxes keep their heights in lines. A number from 0 to 8; anything else counts as 2.

desktopButtons.title: Desktop panel buttons
desktopButtons.description: How the sections view in Claude Desktop draws its pressable titles in the strip and its [+], [-] and [x] icons (desktopPaneScroll sections; every other value and the terminal draw plain). outline: each title a rounded chip bordered in its section's colour, filled softly under the pointer, the shown one filled; each icon a rounded box one row tall bordered the same way, filled under the pointer. plain: bare text. Colours follow desktopStyle (grey under plain). A title that cannot expand stays greyed, in a dim-bordered chip, and not pressable. Dark mode only. Any other value counts as outline.

desktopFont.title: Desktop panel font
desktopFont.description: The font colour and style per section of the sections view in Claude Desktop (desktopPaneScroll sections; every other value and the terminal draw standard): each section's title, its rows and its dim rows, and its title in the strip while it is the one shown. accent: the title in its section's hue and heavier, the rows in a light step of the hue, the dim rows in a muted step of it and italic, the shown title light, bold and underlined. standard: as before, the titles bold in the text colour, the rows in the text colour or dim. A pressable row keeps the text colour; under desktopStyle plain accent adds weights and styles only, no colour. Hues as desktopStyle's: sessions blue, queued work violet, open points sand, the log grey. Any other value counts as accent.

desktopAnimation.title: Desktop panel animation
desktopAnimation.description: How the sections view in Claude Desktop (desktopPaneScroll sections, docked) goes from its three boxes to a section's page and back: smooth (the default): 15 frames, one every 100 ms (1.4 s). off: at once, as before. In each step the section's box grows by an equal share from its even height to the whole panel and the other two shrink by the same share (a box too small for its borders and title is left out); the last frame is the page. A collapse runs the same steps backwards. During a step the growing box shows [-] while it expands and [+] while it collapses: pressing it turns the animation back from the step it reached; any other press ends the animation at once and then acts as usual. From one page to another, and to or from a log, stays instant. Every other desktopPaneScroll value, the panel seated inline and the terminal stay instant. Any other value counts as smooth.
